preview.intro: Two research internships in experimental physics, within groups affiliated to the LHCb and ATLAS collaborations, taught me to build full analysis pipelines: data acquisition, cleaning, statistical modelling, reporting. Python and C++ are my main tools. ROOT, NumPy, Pandas, and scikit-learn are part of my daily workflow.
preview.whatIBuild: Most of my projects start from a need of my own. I run a Proxmox server at home, and the JellyUX Jellyfin plugins grew out of using it. TimePredict comes from my trail running, Accred from the film festivals I attend. This site is one of those projects and has its own page.

full.intro: I hold a Master's in fundamental physics from Université Clermont Auvergne and a university diploma in Data Science. My two research internships, at LPC Clermont in teams from the LHCb and then ATLAS collaborations, taught me to build a full analysis in C++ and Python, from data selection to uncertainty estimates. Since then I have applied the same method to software projects I run on my own.
full.experience: During my Master's, I worked at LPC Clermont, in teams from the LHCb and ATLAS collaborations, on datasets running into terabytes. That is where I learned to build complete analysis pipelines.
full.goals: I'm looking for a role between research and engineering, where data analysis and software development work on the same problem.
